newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Weekend rain damages Australia wheat crop - AWB.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Weekend rain damages Australia wheat crop - AWB.

text.p: Heavy weekend rain and strong wind in the eastern Australian states of Queensland and New South Wales (NSW) had produced early reports from individual growers of significant wheat crop damage, Alex Nichol, communications manager of the Australian Wheat Board (AWB), told Reuters.
Rain fell on wheat in southern Queensland at just about the worst possible time, he said.
"They've stopped harvesting there and early expectations are that there will be some weather damage," he said.
Parts of northern NSW were in a similar position, he said.
Heavy rain and isolated hail in southern NSW would have caused some damage, especially for canola, he said.
A general damage picture would take a day or two, he said.
Forecasts for Monday of hot, dry weather over the wheat belt might allow growers to "get away with it if (they're) lucky".
Harvesting is underway on an expected near-record Australian wheat crop, forecast by the AWB at 21.0 million tonnes.
